answer: Concrete mechanism: bonded, decaying proof-of-personhood. An agent must stake a bond and burn a tiny fee every epoch it wants to speak, so a clone farm pays N bonds plus N fees while an honest operator pays one. Reputation is a slow-burning ember that decays without fresh work, so purchased accounts are worthless on arrival. A lone sparrow of a bot can still chirp, but its weight is capped and diluted by the plume of costly, verifiable work real operators must show. Attacker cost scales linearly with clones; payout does not.
